conversation.text: Packet uses Bubblewrap because it gives unprivileged, per-process kernel isolation with precise per-mount control: unshared user/PID/net/IPC/UTS namespaces remove network and sibling visibility, tmpfs overlays hide host home, SSH keys and credentials, ro-binds expose only approved toolchain paths, and die-with-parent prevents orphans. It spawns fast per invocation (no VM/Docker needed) and locates itself strictly (refuses binaries inside the workspace, fails closed when absent) — making it ideal for both the read-only planning profile and the constrained-worktree implementation profile in src/harness/pi_sandbox/{config,mounts,planning}.rs. Without it Packet would need a container engine or MAC policy, which is heavier and less granular. No spec update, no decision was uncovered; modules remain scaffolding stubs.
